questions.prompt: How do the CPUs and device controllers reach shared memory?
options: Each one has a private cable to memory
They don't: only the CPU can touch memory

questions.prompt: The CPU and I/O devices can execute concurrently.

Who moves data between main memory and a controller's local buffer (without DMA)?
How does a device controller tell the CPU it has finished its operation? It causes an ______. (one word)
What does a device driver give the rest of the kernel?
options: A uniform interface to a device controller

questions.prompt: A single device controller can only ever control one device.
Why do the CPU and devices "compete for memory cycles"?
options: The CPU erases memory between cycles
They all reach memory over the same shared bus, so only one can use it at a time
Devices are not allowed to read memory
Memory is too small to hold all their data
